column2: Thank you for playing. The rest of the climb continues in the full game.
The main save was damaged; your progress was recovered from the backup copy.
The fog thickens: only what is near can be seen.
Chains hang from the ceiling. Lure the enemies into the sweep.
Shh. It is over. I have you.
You fall, and I remake you. We have done this before, you and I. Long before.
Look: someone comes out of the mist. Do not fear, I know him. An ancient king, and kind. He means you no harm.
Lost spark... how good that you woke. The threshold has one law: none pass but those who touch me with their light.
(raises the orb; the mask lights up) Show me yours. Come.
Seven Archons, seven Rings. Gather them all, and I will show you how to undo this world of lies.
The Archon here will offer you what you lost. Remember: a copy is not a return.
He will offer you power: the oldest of lies, and the sweetest.
Everything rots, Bearer. I watched all I planted die. Surrender now, and I will spare you the end.
Guardian of the Shrine of Torpor
Guardian of the Shrine of Hunger
Guardian of the Shrine of the Chain
Guardian of the Shrine of Silence
Guardian of the Shrine of the Mirror
Guardian of the Shrine of Blight
Guardian of the Shrine of the Crown
Give me one! One memory that is mine!
(the stitches burst) Someone answered him once, from up above. I heard it. He sewed me shut for it.
Galila classified you, and lost. Four to go.
Here I fall quiet. You speak, today. I will listen.
I gave you a grief so I could give you a path. Grief is the softest of collars.
You wept for me. The seven were my children, and you brought me what was left of them.
Galila does not hate you. He classifies you. That is worse.
You came from me. I found you. Do not forget the order of things.
Astaphaios will give you what you want most: you, before everything. The cruelest blow.
Five Rings. Two more, and I will show you the end of all this.
Defeat the King at the Threshold.
Defeat Athoth, the Archon of Torpor.
Defeat Harmas, the Archon of Hunger.
Defeat Galila, the Archon of the Chain.
Defeat Yabel, the Archon of Silence.
Defeat Astaphaios, the Archon of the Mirror.
Defeat Belias, the Archon of Blight.
Defeat Armupiel, the Archon of the Crown.
Defeat Athoth without falling once in the journey.
Defeat an Archon without taking damage on their screen.
Raise the weapon to its maximum level.
Awaken 4 Sleepers in a single journey.
Find every creature along the way.
Recover the 7 memory shards in the Center.
Finish the journey on Hard or above.
The spark who woke without memory at the Threshold.
She crosses the seven Aeons to remember who she is.
The weapon awakens at the shrines: each level opens new combos.
Scraps of light the Kenoma has not finished putting out.
They crawl toward wherever there is still warmth.
Weak and slow: a light combo settles it.
A spark that forgot its own name.
It wanders fast and aimless, chasing whoever still shines.
Fast: let the lunge pass, then answer.
Forged from hyle and obedience by the Demiurge.
It carries its blade the way one carries an order.
Parry the golden strike and punish the opening.
A larva that kept too much fire.
It runs to the nearest light and bursts into flame.
The blast cannot be parried: dodge.
A thorn-shelled guardian, posted at the gates of the Aeons.
Slow to rise, heavy to fall.
When it raises its arms, get clear: the blow crushes the ground.
A beast bred to sniff out sparks.
It does not bark. It charges.
Dodge the charge and strike while it skids to a halt.
A horned reaper that gathers light like ripe wheat.
It holds no anger; it only reaps.
Parry the golden strike and answer with the combo.
It guards the Seal with a shield that knows no weariness.
Behind it, order; before it, no one.
Light strikes hit the shield: use a heavy strike or a spell.
A watcher of the Kenoma's low skies.
From on high, it aims and fires.
It shoots from afar: close in between one shot and the next.
A mass of iron that obeys without asking.
Each step makes the ground remember its own weight.
Do not trade blows with it: dodge the slam and come back.
It heralds Silence with a crown and a staff.
The voice never arrives; only the shot.
It shoots from afar: close the distance and keep striking.
An echo of the void that cannot decide where it is.
It vanishes before its prey and appears at its back.
When it vanishes, turn around: it reappears behind you.
It sows the ground with larvae and prays for them.
It prefers distance and a crowd.
Take it down first, before the ground fills with larvae.
A form the Kenoma began and gave up on finishing.
It charges hard: dodge and counter.
It walks asleep through the catacombs of Torpor.
It yawns, and whoever breathes the yawn grows heavy.
Stay out of the yawn's path: it slows you down.
Hunger made flesh, with a mouth where its chest should be.
It is never full; only less hungry.
Every bite that lands heals it: do not let it bite.
No one knows what they are accused of; neither does he.
His chain never lets go of what it holds.
The chain pins you in place: dodge when he throws it.
He guards the library of blank books.
His mouth sewn shut; his silence, contagious.
Near him, spells fall silent: fight with the weapon.
The Mirror returns everything, even the blow.
It pulls back at the exact instant of the attack.
It recoils from the first strike: press in and chain the combo.
It carries Blight on its back, like a rotten garden.
When it falls it leaves a pool of poison: move away from it.
It turns its back on no one.
From the front only heavy strikes wound it: attack from behind.
The Mirror strips her of her form and fills it with void.
It fights like her, and faster than her.
Do not trade blows: parry and answer.
Athoth, Archon of Torpor, offers sleep the way one offers shelter.
Get out of the fog: inside it you are slowed.
Harmas, Archon of Hunger, sells everything that is missing.
An endless mouth where the torso should be.
When he starts to suck in, move away before the slam.
Galila, Archon of the Chain, classifies, judges and binds.
Every law longs for a chain.
The chain pins you in place: dodge the throw and the charge.
Yabel, Archon of Silence, does not speak: he only silences.
His aura buries spells in the void.
Inside the aura, use the weapon. Wounded, he appears at your back.
Astaphaios, Archon of the Mirror, returns the words of whoever faces him.
Silver, shards and a “we” that is no one.
Wounded, he calls Sophia's Shadow: do not let it surround you.
Belias, Archon of Blight, mistakes weariness for truth.
Wherever he passes, life forgets to die.
His charge leaves pools of poison: do not fight standing in them.
Armupiel, Archon of the Crown: almost king of everything.
Wounded, he summons servants and shields himself: take the servants down first.
The white priest who guards the Threshold.
Too kind for one who bars a passage.
Parry the golden strikes; dodge the red ones.
The King's mask, with no one left to hold it up.
More fragile and faster than the one at the Threshold.
Read the glow early: the blow arrives sooner.
What lay behind the mask: a hollow giant.
The shards of its face still reflect borrowed light.
Stay out of the slam's reach and strike on its way back.
Yaldabaoth, the Demiurge: he made the Kenoma and called it his.
Blind to all that is not himself.
No weapon is enough on its own: remember what burns.
Soter, the Anointed, walks freely through the Kenoma: the Blind One cannot see him.
He heals, awakens and asks. He never fights.
He does not fight: choose one of the gifts he offers.
Velkar, the Archon who let go of his own chain.
He lost the crown and the post; he kept the guilt.
He does not fight: listen to what he has to say.
In the beginning there was the One. From it the Aeons emanated, in pairs,\nlike overflowing light. There nothing slept. Nothing forgot.
The youngest, Sophia, sought to reach the Source alone.\nFrom that unpartnered desire a formless son was born,\nand she hid him in a cloud.

Blind to the Light, he believed himself the only god and made the Kenoma.
In the clay sleep the sparks he took from his mother.

One of them has just felt pain.
